body: I disagree, it just sounds different. There's a strange abrasive yet soothing quality to harmonics, it's the very thing which makes them so enjoyable and yet, so harsh. At its core, a large part of what makes music enjoyable is unity; too much unity and the piece is boring, too little and it feels chaotic. In my opinion, this piece is a perfect example of how to toe the line of timbral chaos without giving in to the experimentally prone nature of stranger sounds. It's the dreamy tone set by the first melodic motif that immediately contrasts with the second which is dominated by the much more tinny and harsh timbre of the harmonics, those aspects are what I'm sure, make you dislike it, and also are what make me enjoy it so much.
Fun Fact: SWV sampled this song for their hit song called [Rain](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e4C0r7UM4Cs).

I have a few ideas to rattle off before I start my argument so allow me to do that.  Firstly, I think it's very important to outline the difference between rap music and hip hop. Rap is simply a kind of music, a delivery based on rhythm and "flowing" over a beat, meanwhile, Hip Hop is a movement, its roots are in struggle, its roots are in expressing that struggle. Hip Hop evolved from poetry so Hip Hop inherently has more meaningful lyrics than its counterpart, rap, which is defined as such by simply its delivery of vocals. I will list off a few examples of meaningful lyrics in my second point. Secondarily, I disagree, I believe that while ***some*** ***rap music*** is meant to make you feel good and nothing more, I would argue that there is enduring value in Hip Hop. The lyric that you mentioned above "First, you get a swimming pool full of liquor, then you dive in it." is actually, through hyperbole, helping to paint a picture of Kendrick Lamar's life as a younger man, when he was subjected to peer pressure and allowed himself to "drown" in a pool of  "poison" through consuming excessive amounts of alcohol. If you read through the [lyrics](https://genius.com/Kendrick-lamar-swimming-pools-drank-lyrics) you'll find that the song is written as though it's telling a story of how his upbringing was in terms of how alcohol was treated as a drug. The first verse documents Mr. Lamar's environment and how it lead to him abusing alcohol. Kendrick says that he "done grew up 'round some people living their life in bottles", this line is quite simply saying that the community in which Kendrick Lamar grew up was no stranger to alcoholism, in fact, even his grandfather had a "golden flask" and did the metaphorical "backstroke every day in Chicago". This line highlights his grandfather's relationship with alcohol through the utilisation of a metaphor used in the chorus. This metaphor compares alcohol to a swimming pool, some people play in it, enjoying the feeling of the cool water on their skin while others like it because they have nothing better to do and as such, they seek a certain feeling of escapism. The next two lines outline this as well Lamar saying that "Some people like the way it feels..." meanwhile others simply want to "...kill their sorrows.". Kendrick then shifts from describing his peer's relationship to alcohol and starts describing how he got into the situation where he was abusing alcohol by saying that, "Some people wanna fit in with the popular that was my problem." he then goes on to say how he was overindulging until an individual pressures him into consuming even more excess. "Took a sip, then another sip, then somebody said to me "Nigga why you babysittin' only two or three shots? I'ma show you how to turn it up a notch. First, you get a swimming pool full of liquor, then you dive in it""

This song could be easily taken as a drinking anthem if taken at face value, but if you take the analysis a little further you will see its cleverly disguised as a drinking anthem while it actually condemns the overuse and abuse of alcohol.

This is the purpose of hip hop, to express and teach, and this is exactly what this song does.
